steps.instruction: Place the battery on the breadboard power rails.
Build the first branch: connect resistor1 and LED1 in series from positive to negative rail.
Build the second branch: connect resistor2 and LED2 in series from positive to negative rail (separate rows).
Connect the switch on the main negative rail to control both branches.
Close the switch to complete both parallel paths.
Use the multimeter to measure total current from the battery.

rules.feedback: First branch complete: resistor1 → LED1 across the power rails.
Second branch complete: resistor2 → LED2 across the power rails.
Switch connected on the negative rail to control both branches.
Both LEDs light! Each branch gets full voltage independently.
Total current equals the sum of both branch currents.

outcomes.title: Parallel circuit complete
outcomes.description: Two parallel branches each with a resistor and LED. Both LEDs receive full battery voltage and operate independently.

safeFailure.message: The parallel circuit isn't working correctly.
safeFailure.guidance: In a parallel circuit, each branch connects directly across the power rails. Check that both branches have their own complete path.

narration.text: Place the battery on the power rails. Positive to red, negative to blue.
Build the first branch: connect a resistor and LED in series from the positive rail to the negative rail.
Build the second branch on a different row: another resistor and LED from positive to negative rail. Each branch is independent.
Add a switch on the negative rail to control power to both branches at once.
Close the switch. Both LEDs light up! In parallel, each branch gets the full battery voltage.
Measure the total current from the battery. It equals the sum of currents through each branch.

captions.text: First branch: resistor + LED from + to - rail.
Second branch: separate resistor + LED from + to - rail.
Switch on negative rail controls both branches.
Close switch — both LEDs light independently!
Total current = sum of branch currents.
